details.rationale: Weighted score trajectory is healthy (20.5→15.25→15.0→12.5) and v4 resolves 49 prior flags, but two significant correctness defects introduced in v4 are guaranteed runtime failures that block execution. CF-7B50AD8E/CF-1632D304 (tree-hash self-referential defect): Step 15.2 asserts HEAD^{tree} == delivery_tree_hash, but recording the tree hash in the handoff changes the handoff bytes, which changes the tree content, which changes the tree hash — the assertion is mathematically unsatisfiable (same chicken-and-egg the plan correctly acknowledged for commit hashes but failed to recognize for tree hashes). The fix is to move the delivery TREE hash to the same gitignored sidecar + git note as the delivery COMMIT hash; the committed handoff records only baseline commit+tree hashes. CF-50DE2C/CF-61A4C1 (ReconciliationResult name collision): the plan uses ReconciliationResult(status=..., issues=..., attempt_id=...) but an existing incompatible ReconciliationResult dataclass at arnold/workflow/effect_reconciliation.py:84 has fields (verdict: ReconciliationVerdict, provider_idempotency_key, evidence_payload, query_failure, is_authoritative, provider_version). The plan must explicitly declare a new disambiguated type (e.g., LedgerReconciliationResult) in persistence_service.py. CF-F716F109 (mixed-attempt authority_scope): per-attempt tag vs per-event cl2_kind discriminator creates ambiguity for attempts containing both v1 and legacy_historical events. All three are fixable in one more iteration. The baseline-resolution gate (Step 0.1) for CF-00D5682C/CF-1508FE is structurally correct — the outcome depends on runtime git state which no plan can fabricate.
warnings: CF-7B50AD8E/CF-1632D304: Tree-hash self-referential defect is a guaranteed runtime failure. Fix: move delivery TREE hash to gitignored sidecar + git note alongside delivery COMMIT hash. Committed handoff records only baseline commit hash + baseline tree hash (both known pre-work, immutable). This mirrors the pattern already correctly used for the commit hash.

CF-50DE2C/CF-61A4C1: ReconciliationResult name collision. Existing arnold/workflow/effect_reconciliation.py:84 ReconciliationResult has incompatible fields (verdict: ReconciliationVerdict, provider_idempotency_key, evidence_payload, query_failure, is_authoritative, provider_version — no status/issues/attempt_id). Fix: declare a new LedgerReconciliationResult dataclass in persistence_service.py with fields (attempt_id: str, status: str, issues: list[str], event_snapshot: dict).

CF-F716F109: Mixed-attempt authority_scope ambiguity. Per-attempt tag (authority_scope) vs per-event discriminator (cl2_kind). Fix: either (a) require legacy records to use distinct attempt_ids from v1 records, or (b) specify authority_scope as per-contribution rather than per-attempt, or (c) add a mixed-attempt test case and define the resolution rule (e.g., authoritative if ANY v1 record present).

settled_decisions.decision: CL1 domain objects ride as payload content on EXTERNAL_EFFECT_OUTCOME events distinguished by cl2_kind discriminator (occurrence|reconciliation|disposition|legacy_historical), not as lifecycle event types
settled_decisions.rationale: Store's AttemptEventType precedence rules (RECONCILIATION requires prior PERSISTENCE_FAILED, COMPLETED is terminal with exactly-one-terminal guard) block one-to-one mapping. Verified at execution_attempt_ledger.py:212-234.

settled_decisions.decision: Schema-version conflict resolved by filter-and-tag, not upgrade: legacy records preserved with original schema_version, tagged cl2_kind=legacy_historical + metadata.derived_from_legacy=true, excluded from replay by 3-condition conjunctive filter (exclude-then-reconstruct order)
settled_decisions.rationale: Honors both 'preserves all available legacy evidence' (persisted, queryable via read_legacy_context) and 'rejects unsupported target versions without partial publish' (non-v1 records never enter v1 replay pipeline). North Star immutability clause forbids version rewriting.

settled_decisions.decision: OneTimeImporter bypasses persist_occurrence and builds LedgerEvent payloads directly via store.append_event with cl2_kind=legacy_historical
settled_decisions.rationale: persist_occurrence validates via CritiqueOccurrenceEnvelope.from_dict which rejects non-v1 schema_version (schemas.py:263-268, SUPPORTED_VERSIONS={'cl.schema.v1'}). Legacy records with original non-v1 version strings cannot pass from_dict.

settled_decisions.decision: UNAVAILABLE encoding on legacy records is a labeling convention, NOT a fails-closed guard; cl2_kind=legacy_historical discriminator is the sole operative defense excluding legacy records from replay
settled_decisions.rationale: Verified at source: FailureMode.BRIEFING_INPUT_UNAVAILABLE (semantic_loop.py:1068) requires required_for_briefing=True (not set by importer); FailureMode.CUSTODY_UNAVAILABLE_EVIDENCE (semantic_loop.py:206) requires both unavailable_reason AND reopen_condition (only former is set). Neither path is operative; cl2_kind filter is the sole defense.

settled_decisions.decision: Restart reconciliation uses two distinct store APIs: validate_ledger_event_ordering (returns list[str]) for ordering/precedence violations mapped to status=ordering_violation, and store.query_gaps (returns list[GapEntry]) for non-contiguous sequence gaps mapped to status=sequence_gap
settled_decisions.rationale: validate_ledger_event_ordering does NOT detect sequence gaps — confirmed by module's Known Limitation docstring (execution_attempt_ledger.py:46-65) and monotonicity check only testing sequence <= prev_sequence, never sequence != prev_sequence + 1. The two APIs serve distinct purposes with distinct ReconciliationResult status values.
